def-qc-tqc-physical-braid-interface:
## Definition

Let $V$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space and let
$\rho:B_n\to U(V)$ be a fixed mathematical braid representation. A **physical
implementation record** for a braid $b\in B_n$ consists of all of the following
data and hypotheses:

1. a finite-dimensional physical state space identified with $V$ on a specified
   low-energy sector;
2. a $C^2$ path $H(s)$ of Hermitian endomorphisms, $0\le s\le1$, and a
   norm-continuous constant-rank orthogonal spectral projection $P(s)$ that
   selects the followed band and is separated from its complement by a
   uniform positive full gap;
3. an explicit initial preparation isometry into $\operatorname{ran}P(0)$ and
   a stated slow-time schedule $T>0;$
4. a separate identification of the band's transported action for the chosen
   exchange path with $\rho(b)$, up to a stated scalar phase.

The first three clauses form an instance of the finite adiabatic path model
[[def-qa-36-finite-adiabatic-path-model]]. Under those hypotheses,
[[thm-qa-36-jrs-finite-adiabatic-bound]] bounds the deviation from ideal
adiabatic band following. That estimate does not establish that a material
realizes the fusion category, that the exchange path has the prescribed
holonomy, or that the initial state can be prepared at no cost. Locality,
temperature, quasiparticle separation, stray excitations, and tunnelling
require their own physical error model.
lem-qc-tqc-special-unitary-connected:
## Statement

For every integer $n\ge1$, the matrix group
$$SU(n)=\{A\in M_n(\mathbb C):A^*A=I,\ \det A=1\}$$
is path connected.
def-qc-tqc-fixed-charge-encoding:
## Definition

Let $V=V(x^n\to c)\ne0$ be the finite-dimensional fixed-total-charge fusion
space for $n$ identical charges $x$, equipped with the unitary fusion-tree
inner product from [[def-qc-tqc-fusion-tree-basis]]. Let
$\mathcal C=\mathbb C^k$ with its ordered orthonormal computational basis,
where $k\ge1$. A **fixed-charge encoding** is an isometry
$J:\mathcal C\to V$, so $J^*J=I_{\mathcal C}$. Its code subspace is
$J\mathcal C$, and its code projector is
$$P:=JJ^*:V\to V.$$
An encoding records a chosen subspace of a fusion space; it does not identify
that subspace with an object of the fusion category.
def-qc-tqc-logical-error-and-leakage:
## Definition

Let $J:\mathcal C\to V$ be a fixed-charge encoding, $P=JJ^*$ its code
projector, $U\in U(\mathcal C)$ a logical target, and $W\in U(V)$ an ambient
unitary. Its zero-on-the-complement target extension is
$\widetilde U:=JUJ^*:V\to V$. Define the **logical block error** and
**leakage amplitude** by
$$\epsilon_{\mathrm{log}}(W,U):=\|PWP-\widetilde U\|_{\mathrm{op}}, \qquad \epsilon_{\mathrm{leak}}(W):=\|(I-P)WP\|_{\mathrm{op}}.$$
Both are finite operator norms. The first measures the compressed block
against the target; the second measures transfer from the code into its
orthogonal complement. They diagnose different errors.
def-qc-tqc-braid-action-from-fusion-data:
## Definition

Let $x$ be a simple charge in a unitary braided fusion category, let $n\ge2$,
and fix a total charge $c$ with nonzero multiplicity space
$V(x^n\to c)$. Use the left-associated fusion-tree basis. For the Artin
generator $\sigma_i$ that exchanges the $i$th and $(i+1)$st strands, let
$T_i$ be the specified sequence of $F$-moves that changes from the fixed tree
basis to a basis where those two charges fuse first, and let $R_i$ apply the
corresponding $R$-symbol on each pair-charge channel. Define
$$\rho_c(\sigma_i):=T_i^{-1}R_iT_i.$$
This defines the generator assignment. The next theorem proves that the
assignment descends from words to a well-defined group homomorphism. Word
products use matrix multiplication acting right-to-left on column vectors.
The abstract group in this definition is the Artin group
[[def-braid-group-by-the-artin-presentation]]; the positive crossing is the
generator convention used for the displayed $R$-symbols. If a motion is
described chronologically, its matrix product is written in reverse temporal
order.
lem-qc-tqc-zero-logical-error-forces-zer:
## Statement

Let $J:\mathcal C\to V$ be an isometric encoding with $P=JJ^*$, let $U$ be
unitary on $\mathcal C$, and let $W$ be unitary on $V$. If the logical block
error $\|PWP-JUJ^*\|_{\mathrm{op}}$ is zero, then the leakage amplitude
$\|(I-P)WP\|_{\mathrm{op}}$ is zero.
thm-qc-tqc-block-approximation-error:
## Statement

Let $V=P V\oplus(I-P)V$ be an orthogonal decomposition of a finite-dimensional
Hilbert space, let $U$ and $W$ be unitary operators on the two summands, and
let $T:=U\oplus W$. If an ambient unitary $G$ satisfies
$\|G-T\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\delta$, then the logical block error of $G$ relative
to $U$ and its leakage amplitude both are at most $\delta$.
def-qc-tqc-ising-majorana-interface:
## Definition

Let $m\ge2$ and let $\mathcal H=(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes m}$. A **Majorana
system of length $2m$** is a family of operators
$\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_{2m}\in\operatorname{End}(\mathcal H)$ satisfying
$$\gamma_j^*=\gamma_j,\qquad \gamma_j^2=I,\qquad \gamma_j\gamma_k=-\gamma_k\gamma_j\quad(j\ne k).$$
Its parity operator is $\Pi=i^m\gamma_1\cdots\gamma_{2m}$. For each adjacent
pair, put
$$Q_1(j)=\frac{I-i\gamma_j\gamma_{j+1}}2,\qquad Q_\psi(j)=\frac{I+i\gamma_j\gamma_{j+1}}2,\qquad U_j=\exp\!\left(-\frac\pi4\gamma_j\gamma_{j+1}\right).$$

A **Majorana–Ising exchange interface** on a fixed parity sector consists of
such a system, a choice $\eta\in\{1,-1\}$ and the sector
$\mathcal H_\eta=\ker(\Pi-\eta I)$, together with the following explicit
model-identification hypotheses for every $1\le j<2m$: the Ising pair-charge
projections are identified with $Q_1(j),Q_\psi(j)$, and the exchange is
$R_1Q_1(j)+R_\psi Q_\psi(j)$ with the same relative phase
$R_\psi/R_1=i$. The last identity is required for all adjacent pairs as part
of the interface; the three-anyon supplier below establishes it only in its
stated sector and does not prove this all-$m$ identification.
def-qc-tqc-projective-gate-and-metric:
## Definition

Let $V\ne0$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space and let
$U(V)$ be its unitary group. Two unitaries are **projectively equivalent**
when $A=zB$ for some $z\in\mathbb C$ with $|z|=1$; write $[A]\in PU(V)$ for
the equivalence class. Define
$$d_P([A],[B]):=\min_{|z|=1}\|A-zB\|_{\mathrm{op}}.$$
This is the distance after quotienting by one common scalar phase. The phase
is minimized over the unit circle; it is not chosen independently in
different charge blocks.
def-qc-tqc-six-anyon-encoded-subspace:
## Definition

Assume the Fibonacci fusion rules
$1\otimes x=x\otimes1=x$ and $\tau\otimes\tau=1\oplus\tau$, with each
listed summand of multiplicity one. For six ordered $\tau$ charges, let
$W_a$ be the fixed-input, fixed-total fusion space of total charge
$a\in\{1,\tau\}$ in the tree that first fuses leaves $1,2,3$ and $4,5,6$
separately, then fuses those triple outputs. Let
$V_a$ be the same fixed-charge space in the left-associated tree.

To identify these spaces, write
$A=((\tau_1\otimes\tau_2)\otimes\tau_3)$. Use the object associator
composite
$$g=(\alpha^{-1}_{A\otimes\tau_4,\tau_5,\tau_6}) \circ\alpha^{-1}_{A,\tau_4,\tau_5\otimes\tau_6} \circ(\operatorname{id}_A\otimes\alpha_{\tau_4,\tau_5,\tau_6})$$
from the triple-grouped input tree to the left-associated tree. On a fusion
morphism $f$ into $a$, define $G_a(f)=f\circ g^{-1}:V_a$; this is a unitary
change of fusion-tree coordinates.

For one triple of total charge $\tau$, its two orthonormal path vectors are
indexed by the charge $x\in\{1,\tau\}$ after the first two anyons: both
$x\otimes\tau\to\tau$ channels have multiplicity one. Write these vectors as
$|x\rangle$. For $x,y\in\{1,\tau\}$ and $a\in\{1,\tau\}$, let $|x,y;a\rangle$
be the grouped-tree vector with first triple path $x$, first triple total
$\tau$, second triple path $y$, second triple total $\tau$, and final vertex
channel $\tau\otimes\tau\to a$. The last channel has multiplicity one. Define
$$\mathcal C_a:=G_a\bigl(\operatorname{span}\{|x,y;a\rangle: x,y\in\{1,\tau\}\}\bigr)\subseteq V_a.$$
In the ordered basis
$(G_a|1,1;a\rangle,G_a|1,\tau;a\rangle,
G_a|\tau,1;a\rangle,G_a|\tau,\tau;a\rangle)$, the inclusion
$J_a:\mathbb C^4\to V_a$ is an isometry; its code projector is $P_a=J_aJ_a^*$.
The same ordered local triple paths are used for $a=1$ and $a=\tau$; only
the final pair-charge coordinate differs. The orthogonal complements are
called leakage spaces.
lem-qc-tqc-determinant-character-phase:
## Statement

Fix the Fibonacci convention with common exchange scalar $R_1$. Let
$e:B_n\to\mathbb Z$ be exponent sum, sending each Artin generator $\sigma_i$
to $1$. If $\widetilde\rho$ is the generator-normalized representation
$\widetilde\rho(\sigma_i)=R_1^{-1}\rho(\sigma_i)$, then for every braid $b$
and every total-charge block,
$$\rho(b)=R_1^{e(b)}\widetilde\rho(b).$$
The scalar is the same on every total-charge block and every spectator
multiplicity. It is a global phase for an uncontrolled fixed-sector
computation; under coherent control it is a relative phase and must be
tracked.
lem-qc-tqc-fibonacci-b6-path-projectors-:
## Statement

Use the Fibonacci fusion rule $\tau\otimes\tau=1\oplus\tau$ and the
fixed-chirality data
$F^{\tau\tau\tau}_\tau=\begin{pmatrix}\phi^{-1}&\phi^{-1/2}\\
\phi^{-1/2}&-\phi^{-1}\end{pmatrix}$ and
$r=R_\tau/R_1=e^{-3\pi i/5}$. The fixed-total-charge B6 path bases are

$$\mathcal P_1=\{0101010,0101110,0110110,0111010,0111110\},$$

$$\mathcal P_\tau=\{0101011,0101101,0101111,0110101,0110111,0111011,0111101,0111111\},$$

where each path is $(x_0,\ldots,x_6)$, $x_0=0$ is the unit label,
$x_1=1$ is $\tau$, and adjacent labels obey the fusion rule. For
$d_0=1,d_1=\phi$, define $E_i$ on either path basis by
$$(E_i)_{x,y}= \begin{cases} \sqrt{d_{x_i}d_{y_i}}/d_{x_{i-1}}, &x_j=y_j\ (j\ne i),\ x_{i-1}=x_{i+1}=y_{i-1}=y_{i+1},\\ 0,&\text{otherwise,} \end{cases} \qquad P_i:=\phi^{-1}E_i.$$
Then $P_i$ are orthogonal projections, have ranks $2$ on $\mathcal P_1$
and $3$ on $\mathcal P_\tau$, satisfy
$P_iP_{i+1}P_i=\phi^{-2}P_i$ and commute at separation at least two.
Consequently $B_i=rI+(1-r)P_i$ are unitary matrices satisfying the Artin
relations of $B_6$, with
$\det B_i=r^3$ on $V(\tau^6\to1)$ and $\det B_i=r^5$ on
$V(\tau^6\to\tau)$.
lem-qc-tqc-fibonacci-coefficient-ring-sp:
## Statement

Let $r=e^{-3\pi i/5}$, $\phi=(1+\sqrt5)/2=1-r-r^{-1}$, and
$s=\sqrt\phi>0$. Then
$$\mathbb Z[r,s]\cong \mathbb Z[x,y]\big/\bigl(x^4-x^3+x^2-x+1,\ y^2-(1-x-x^{-1})\bigr),$$
where $x^{-1}=x^9$. The assignment
$$r\mapsto15,\qquad r^{-1}\mapsto29,\qquad \phi\mapsto19,\qquad s\mapsto9$$
defines a ring homomorphism to $\mathbb F_{31}$. The elements $r$ and
$\phi$ map to nonzero units, and conjugation of coefficients is handled by
$r\mapsto r^{-1}$ before reduction.
lem-qc-tqc-leakage-logical-error-accumul:
## Statement

Let $P$ be a code projection on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space $V$. Let
$W_1,\ldots,W_G$ be ideal unitaries preserving $\operatorname{ran}P$, and let
$V_1,\ldots,V_G$ be physical unitaries with
$\|V_j-W_j\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\delta_j$. If
$V_{\mathrm{tot}}=V_G\cdots V_1$ and $W_{\mathrm{tot}}=W_G\cdots W_1$,
then, with empty products equal to $I$ and empty sums equal to $0$,
$$\|V_{\mathrm{tot}}-W_{\mathrm{tot}}\|_{\mathrm{op}} \le\sum_{j=1}^{G}\delta_j.$$
Consequently the logical block error and leakage amplitude relative to the
code action of $W_{\mathrm{tot}}$ are each at most $\sum_j\delta_j$.
thm-qc-tqc-braid-action-unitary-and-arti:
## Statement

For a unitary braided fusion category, a simple charge $x$, and a fixed total
charge $c$, the operators in
[[def-qc-tqc-braid-action-from-fusion-data]] define a unitary group
homomorphism
$$\rho_c:B_n\longrightarrow U(V(x^n\to c)).$$
In particular, the adjacent Artin relations and distant commutation relations
hold in each fixed-charge block.
def-qc-tqc-universality-notions:
## Definition

Let $\Gamma\le U(V)$ be a subgroup acting on a nonzero finite-dimensional
Hilbert space $V$. It is **exactly universal** on $V$ when $\Gamma=U(V)$,
**projectively exactly universal** when its image in $PU(V)$ is all of
$PU(V)$, and **projectively dense** when that image is dense in the metric
$d_P$ of [[def-qc-tqc-projective-gate-and-metric]].

For an encoding $J:\mathcal C\to V$ with code projector $P=JJ^*$, the action
is **approximate logical-and-leakage universal** if for every
$U\in U(\mathcal C)$ and every $\epsilon>0$ there is $W\in\Gamma$ and a
phase $z\in U(1)$ such that
$$\|PWP-zJUJ^*\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\epsilon,\qquad \|(I-P)WP\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\epsilon.$$
This last notion includes a leakage bound as a separate requirement; projective
density on one fusion block alone does not supply it.
lem-qc-tqc-pu2-is-so3:
## Statement

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Give $PU(2)$ the quotient metric from
[[def-qc-tqc-projective-gate-and-metric]]. The map
$$q:SU(2)\longrightarrow PU(2),\qquad q(A)=[A],$$
is a two-sheeted covering with kernel $\{I,-I\}$. It induces a topological
group isomorphism $SU(2)/\{\pm I\}\cong PU(2)\cong SO(3)$.
thm-qc-tqc-b6-su5-density:
## Statement

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. In the normalized Fibonacci B6 representation on
$V(\tau^6\to1)\cong\mathbb C^5$, the closure of the braid image in $U(5)$
contains $SU(5)$.
thm-qc-tqc-b6-su8-density:
## Statement

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. In the normalized Fibonacci B6 representation on
$V(\tau^6\to\tau)\cong\mathbb C^8$, the closure of the braid image in $U(8)$
contains $SU(8)$.
thm-qc-tqc-ising-braids-clifford-only:
## Statement

Assume a Majorana–Ising exchange interface as defined in
[[def-qc-tqc-ising-majorana-interface]]. Let
$\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_{2m}$ be Majorana operators on the
$2^m$-dimensional fermionic Fock space, with
$\gamma_j^*=\gamma_j$, $\gamma_j^2=I$, and
$\gamma_j\gamma_k=-\gamma_k\gamma_j$ for $j\ne k$. On either fixed
eigenspace of the total parity
$$\Pi=i^m\gamma_1\gamma_2\cdots\gamma_{2m},$$
the adjacent Ising exchanges, up to their common physical scalar, are
$$U_j=\exp(-\pi\gamma_j\gamma_{j+1}/4),\qquad 1\le j<2m.$$
For $m\ge2$ they normalize the logical Pauli group on the $m-1$ encoded
qubits. Their braid-only projective image is finite and is not dense in
$PU(2^{m-1})$.
lem-qc-tqc-b6-joint-su5-su8-density:
## Statement

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For the normalized simultaneous six-$\tau$
Fibonacci B6 representation on
$V(\tau^6\to1)\oplus V(\tau^6\to\tau)\cong\mathbb C^5\oplus\mathbb C^8$,
the closure in $U(5)\times U(8)$ contains $SU(5)\times SU(8)$.
thm-qc-tqc-fibonacci-single-qubit-densit:
## Statement

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $B_1,B_2$ be the projective Fibonacci generators on the two-dimensional
three-$\tau$, total-$\tau$ fusion space from
[[ex-qc-tqc-fibonacci-qubit-matrices]]. The subgroup they generate is dense
in $PU(2)$.
lem-qc-tqc-su2-determinant-lifts-dense:
## Statement

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $q:SU(2)\to PU(2)$ be the quotient by
$\{\pm I\}$, and let $\Gamma\le PU(2)$ be dense. Then the full inverse image
$q^{-1}(\Gamma)$ is dense in $SU(2)$. Thus projective density gives
determinant-one lifts arbitrarily close to any $SU(2)$ target, while the
choice of a lift can differ by the central sign.
thm-qc-tqc-approximate-encoded-two-qubit:
## Statement

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $U\in U(\mathbb C^4)$ and $\delta>0$.
There is one normalized six-strand Fibonacci braid word $b$ such that its
actions $B_1(b)$ and $B_\tau(b)$ on the total-charge-$1$ and total-charge-$\tau$
blocks are simultaneously within $\delta$ of
$$T_1=U\oplus(\det U)^{-1}\in SU(5),\qquad T_\tau=U\oplus\operatorname{diag}((\det U)^{-1},1,1,1)\in SU(8).$$
For the triple-triple computational subspace in either block, the logical
block error and leakage amplitude are each at most $\delta$. The corresponding
physical categorical braid differs from the normalized word by the common
scalar phase specified by
[[lem-qc-tqc-determinant-character-phase]].
thm-qc-tqc-spectator-extension:
## Statement

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, $n\ge2$, and a total charge $c$ with
$V(\tau^n\to c)\ne0$. The code in $3n$ $\tau$ anyons factors as
$\mathcal C_n\cong(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes n}\otimes V(\tau^n\to c)$.
For any adjacent pair of encoded triples, any $U\in U(4)$, and any
$\delta>0$, one normalized six-strand braid induces an ambient operator
within $\delta$ of the code-preserving ideal extension of $U$ on the entire
fixed-charge space $V(\tau^{3n}\to c)$. Consequently its logical block error
and leakage amplitude are each at most $\delta$, uniformly over all
spectator fusion paths and states that already have a component outside the
code.
thm-qc-tqc-arbitrary-n-register-universa:
## Statement

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For every $n\ge1$, every total charge $c$ with
$V(\tau^n\to c)\ne0$, every unitary $U$ on $n$ logical qubits, and every
$\epsilon>0$, the triple-$\tau$ code
$$(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes n}\otimes V(\tau^n\to c)$$
admits a finite normalized braid word $V_b$ such that
$$\inf_{|z|=1}\|P_{\rm code}V_bP_{\rm code} -zJ(U\otimes I_S)J^*\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\epsilon,\qquad \|(I-P_{\rm code})V_bP_{\rm code}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\epsilon.$$
Here $S=V(\tau^n\to c)$ is the spectator space, $J:(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes n}\otimes S\to V(\tau^{3n}\to c)$ is the isometric triple-code inclusion, and the logical target is lifted as $U\otimes I_S$. The bounds are uniform over spectator fusion states. No efficient braid
word-length, search-time, or finite-precision bound is asserted.
